<reason>Both sides were skilled and the clash narrowed properly. CON built a genuinely live route: the motion's single criterion (predictive validity) is the wrong currency for a non-selection offsite, the counterfactual to a ban is unexamined gut feel, and "blunt" is a case for reform rather than abolition. Its best original move — DISC's deliberately non-evaluative frame licenses disclosure in a way a Big Five score-report does not — was fresh and forced PRO to work. But PRO held a cleaner spine across all rounds: unreliability at the letter level, the rule that any tool asserting facts about a person must back them, and above all the dilemma that every benefit CON names survives removing the product while only the labels do not. PRO's dilemma on the thermometer defence (if the retreat runs on letters, it runs on rounding error; if on continuous scores, it is a Big Five inventory) was answered by CON only by relocating the value in the framing, and PRO's reply that "the specifics carry it" locates the value in the part that is not the typology landed hard. Decisively, CON's honest but costly concession that results should shape interviews, onboarding and team placement handed PRO the hiring half: an invalid score moving a real decision. PRO also handled pressure questions directly with clean A1:/A2: structure and a plausible account of who opens the conversation without a vendor. CON's closing reframe — replaceability is not invalidity — was sharp and got the last word, but PRO had already supplied affirmative harms (labels hardening into ceilings, laundering typecasting, documented invalid criteria as a plaintiff's exhibit) that make stopping worthwhile even for a merely replaceable tool. PRO's late "structured interview template costs less than the vendor" is a mild closing add-on but narrow.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>PRO's turn on CON's own sentence — "the letters open the conversation; the specifics carry it" — reframed CON's defence as locating all the value in the non-MBTI part and all the defect in the MBTI part, reinforced by the dilemma that reading continuous scores just means using a Big Five inventory. Paired with PRO's exploitation of CON's concession that results should influence team placement, this squeezed CON's remaining ground to a benefit that survives abolition.</best_rebuttal>
